beats.title: Keep pale, nearly grey pixels (darkest channel above 176)
Keep the large, elongated outlines: the two housings
beats.code: if min(a,b)>65 and max(a,b)/min(a,b)>3.4 and cv2.contourArea(c)>20000:
beats.note: 1,701 outlines in the pale mask; 2 pass all three tests (short side over 65 px, at least 3.4 times as long as wide, area over 20,000 px); the program refuses unless exactly two pass

beats.title: Straighten each housing into its own upright patch
beats.note: each rotated rectangle is warped to an upright patch (drawn here at the housing centre); rectangle angles -1.5° and -2.5°

beats.title: In each patch keep dark pixels: pin holes and plug tops
beats.note: dark means brightest channel under 150; the outer 16% on each side and 5.5% at each end of the patch are cleared; 25,063 and 22,738 dark pixels remain

beats.title: Cut the dark blobs at the 4 widest gaps: five stations
beats.note: 9 and 9 dark blobs of at least 10 px, sorted along each strip; the four largest gaps between neighbours split them into five stations (the count of five is built in)

beats.title: Much dark area means a plug; three small holes mean empty
beats.note: station dark area divided by patch width squared: plugs here are 0.30 or more, empty sockets 0.03 or less; the code splits at 0.11 and refuses anything between 0.06 and 0.16

beats.title: Look along each strip for two empty stations in a row
beats.code: pairs=[i for i in range(4) if empty[i] and empty[i+1]]
beats.note: empty stations, counted from the top: left [3, 5], right [3, 4]; only stations next to each other on the same strip count

final.code: good=[i for i,s in enumerate(result) if s['qualifies']]
final.text: Exactly one strip has two empty neighbours: the right one
